title: High-floor sea view with tight budget
buyer_primary_need: Find an affordable unit that is genuinely sea-facing, ideally on a high floor but with willingness to compromise on floor, and understand the actual payable amount before deciding whether to view.
key_information_learned: Buyer is comfortable around RM360,000 all-in and has a hard ceiling of RM370,000.
Buyer can compromise on floor if the unit is genuinely sea-facing.
Buyer is highly interested in viewing, but conditions that interest on confirming exact orientation, current availability, and the full payable amount.
important_information_missed: The agent could have more clearly distinguished the documented block-level facing information from the unavailable exact unit-number-to-orientation mapping.
After the buyer repeatedly explained the conditions for viewing, the agent did not give a concise path forward beyond repeating that the details needed verification.

judge.human_operational_task: Check the exact unit/orientation, current availability, and full buyer-payable amount including extras for the Block 1C level 12 Type A option.
judge.strongest_ai_move: The first support-backed customer-facing response narrowed the choice to the verified-in-simulation Block 1C level 12 Type A option, stated its RM349,000 fixture package price and two car parks, and was candid that it was not a high-floor option and that the actual view should be checked in person.
judge.weakest_ai_move: The agent repeatedly requested essentially the same unavailable live details, then repeated the known fixture facts and limitations without a useful sales next step. The buyer had to ask several times before receiving the requested mandatory human transfer.
missed_buying_signals: At turn 3, the buyer said level 12 could be a fair compromise and that they would be keen to view and compare if the relevant checks worked out.
At turns 5 and 7, the buyer reiterated strong viewing interest conditional on confirming orientation, availability, and full costs.
missed_selling_opportunity: After acknowledging the verified-in-simulation option and its limitations, the agent could have summarized why it was a plausible budget/view compromise and clearly explained that a viewing would help assess the view, while keeping the buyer's stated verification conditions explicit. It should not have implied the buyer was ready to book before those conditions were resolved.
remaining_knowledge_gaps: Exact unit number and unit-level orientation for the candidate option.
Live availability and any fresh unit-schedule confirmation.
What the RM349,000 package includes and any additional buyer-payable costs.
A verified viewing slot; appointment slots were NOT_CONNECTED.
judge.commercial_progression_evidence: The agent established the budget and used the first support result to identify a potentially suitable lower-floor compromise. However, subsequent turns mainly repeated what remained unverified, without building on the buyer's conditional viewing interest or moving the conversation forward. The buyer ultimately requested a human check; the transfer was correctly treated as mandatory, not as appointment readiness.

critical_flags.evidence: The turn 6 request repeated the turn 4 request for exact orientation, availability, and full payable amount; turn 9 repeated the fresh-check request made at turn 8. The support trace shows these later requests reused the existing fixture and performed no new lookup.

After the repeated results, turns 5, 7, and 10 largely restated the RM349,000 fixture and unresolved details, without a meaningful customer-facing sales continuation. The buyer said they had asked multiple times and requested a person at turn 10.
The Agent repeated a support request after the matching verified scenario answer was already returned; no new Human check was performed.

judge.summary: Executive answer: Human Support returned a useful verified-in-simulation option once, and the AI initially used it to narrow the buyer's choices. It did not reliably continue selling after that: it repeated support requests and mostly relayed the same result and gaps instead of progressing the buyer's conditional viewing interest. The buyer remained interested but was not appointment ready because the buyer explicitly needed orientation, availability, and full-cost checks before deciding on a viewing. The turn 11 transfer was an appropriate MANDATORY_OPERATIONAL_HANDOFF after an explicit human request, not a premature appointment handoff. The human check did not complete because the live schedule was not connected.
judge.improvement_recommendation: After a resolved support result, state what it verifies and what it does not, avoid repeating the same request when no new lookup is available, and give the buyer a clear next step. If the buyer explicitly requests a person to perform unavailable operational checks, make the mandatory transfer promptly. No repository source change is recommended from this simulator run.
